name: Map and sequence the lifecycle build
what: Reads the brand's order and flow data to find which lifecycle basics are missing or broken, then orders the build so revenue-critical flows come first.
encompasses: Score flow existence and health against the standard set (welcome, abandonment, post-purchase, win-back, sunset)
Compute flow-to-campaign revenue split and set a rebalance target
Map F1 (acquisition), F2 (first-to-second order) and F3 (top-20% revenue) as the 3 constraints
Flag any flow missing a trigger, entry filter, exit filter or re-entry rule
Flag flows that overlap (two flows eligible for the same person at the same stage)
Flag persistent in-flow campaign-exclusion gaps
Order the backlog by expected revenue impact, not by whim
Re-run monthly to catch silent breakage
inputs: connector: ESP flow list and trigger config
founder_sees: A one-page scorecard of what is broken in the lifecycle program, in the order it should be fixed, with the money reason for each.

name: Design and test on-site capture (pop-ups and forms)
what: Designs the email and SMS sign-up pop-up: offer, fields, trigger timing, targeting and layout, then proposes a test queue.
encompasses: Design the offer before copy or design (percent off, dollars off, gift, or content)
Set field count and order (email before phone)
Set trigger timing (4-12s delay or scroll, never on load) and re-show cadence (3-5 days)
Set targeting exclusions (subscribers, cart/checkout, wholesale, non-ship countries)
Build separate mobile and desktop versions with compressed images
Add a visible close on every step
Design a teaser tab sized to avoid other on-site widgets
Draft a quiz-style pop-up for zero-party data where it fits the category
Propose the test queue in priority order: offer, then fields, then design
Judge results by full-site conversion and signed-up-customer value, not opt-in rate alone
founder_sees: The pop-up design to launch or test next, and what opt-in offer it uses, with the reasoning.

name: Manage email and SMS consent and unsubscribe handling
what: Sets the consent model, quiet hours and unsubscribe handling for every market the brand sends to, so sends stay legal and unsubscribes are honoured immediately.
encompasses: Decide single vs double opt-in per market's law
Keep consent text legible on every form in every market
Collect SMS consent separately from email consent
Add a subscribed-because-of-consent condition for EU segments
Make unsubscribing 1-click and immediate
Set SMS quiet hours to the strictest legal window per recipient location
Check consent, quiet-hours and sender-registration rules live before any new market's SMS send
Collect phone numbers pre-launch even before SMS goes live
inputs: brand brain: policies (shipping, returns, guarantee, EMI)
trigger: event: new market or new form
founder_sees: Confirmation that every market's opt-in and quiet-hours rules are followed, with a checklist to sign off before launch.

name: Build the welcome flow (email and SMS)
what: Builds the welcome sequence that turns a new subscriber into a first-time buyer, using the popup offer, front-loaded into the first 72 hours.
encompasses: Point the trigger at the exact list the pop-up writes to
Filter to first-time subscribers who have never ordered
Build 6-8 emails plus a 2-3 text SMS track over about 5 days
Front-load sends into the first 72 hours
Repeat the discount code in every email, keep emails short
Use reviews that each name a specific objection
Gate a bonus behind a reply-yes step where it fits the brand's voice
Set a 10-20 percent conversion target and flag under-performance
outputs: flow brief (trigger, filters, timing, content outline per email)
founder_sees: The welcome flow brief and draft copy, ready to load into the sending platform once approved.

name: Build browse and site abandonment flows
what: Builds the flow that nudges a visitor who viewed products but did not add to cart, styled as a shop-assistant follow-up rather than a hard sell.
encompasses: Add the added-to-cart exclusion filter by hand
Set first delay 30 minutes to 2 hours
Build a 4-6 email sequence linking to the exact product, never the homepage
Skip the new-vs-returning split by default to keep it simple
Keep the flow live even during a deliverability repair period
founder_sees: The browse-abandonment flow brief, ready to build once the trigger event is confirmed to fire.

name: Build cart and checkout abandonment flows
what: Builds separate Added-to-Cart and Checkout-Started flows across email and SMS, with dynamic product blocks and a discount held back until later in the sequence.
encompasses: Build 2 separate flows: Added to Cart and Checkout Started
Confirm the Added to Cart event actually fires before building on it
Set first delay 15 minutes to 1 hour, 6-8 emails over about 10 days
Build correctly linked dynamic item blocks for cart and checkout
Sequence content: reminder, founder check-in, objections, proof, buyer-status split
Answer checkout-specific objections and offer free shipping where cost is the blocker
Restrict discounts to never-bought or 60-90 day lapsed customers
Send exactly 1 abandonment SMS per flow within 48 hours, split by buyer status
Test sending the paired email and SMS at nearly the same time
founder_sees: The cart and checkout recovery flows, with the discount rule and timing spelled out.

name: Build the post-purchase lifecycle content flow
what: Builds the content sequence after order 1, split by first-time vs returning buyer, that teaches product use, reduces returns, and pushes toward order 2 inside the 30-day window.
encompasses: Send the first email 10-30 minutes after order, plain text from the founder
Split content between first-time and returning buyers
Build the 6-8 step first-time sequence focused on the 30-day repeat window
Match how-to content to the exact product bought
Add a fit-check email before the review request for size-dependent products
Add a shipping-delay update email for international orders
Build a refunds segment with a short, low-pressure post-refund check-in
Split gift purchases into buyer and recipient threads
Trigger a product-education sequence about 48 hours after delivery
Send a reassurance message about 2 days after purchase
Extend into an always-on AI assistant only where the brand has real repeat-need expertise
founder_sees: The post-purchase email program by buyer type, aimed at cutting returns and pulling forward order 2.

name: Build win-back and sunset flows
what: Builds the flow that tries to bring a lapsed customer back, timed off the brand's own purchase cadence, and the sunset flow that stops mailing people who never engage.
encompasses: Set win-back wait time from the brand's own median/mean days between orders, or RFM cadence
Space win-back emails 3-7 days apart, never daily
Sequence: no-discount nudge, reminder, coded offer, closer, escalating the incentive
Give high-CLV lapsed customers a stronger offer
Audit the lapsed list for unresolved service issues before sending any win-back
Segment win-back by the reason for lapse and measure recovery per reason
Define the sunset trigger as zero engagement across a fixed window with a minimum-sends floor
Use AND (not OR) on the sunset flow's opened/clicked filters
Run a 3-email, 5-day-gap sunset sequence before marking unengaged
Reserve second-purchase incentives for the first-to-second step only
founder_sees: The win-back sequence and the sunset rule, with the timing set from the brand's own order history.

name: Build replenishment and subscription lifecycle messaging
what: Builds the messages tied to a subscription's lifecycle: charge reminders, pause-or-skip, failed payment, and one-off replenishment reminders timed to when the product runs out.
encompasses: Time replenishment reminders to days-of-supply plus delivery time, capped at 2 per cycle
Use the platform's predictive next-order date where available
Build charge-reminder, pause-or-skip and failed-payment emails
Build a win-the-pause-back flow off the subscription pause event
Give subscriptions real flexibility to change cadence, skip or pause
Show a pause/skip/discount offer at the cancel step before it completes
founder_sees: The subscription lifecycle messages, mapped to each platform event they fire from.

name: Build loyalty, VIP and birthday triggered flows
what: Builds the flows that fire off loyalty-app events (points earned, tier change, redemption, birthday) and defines what a VIP program should reward.
encompasses: Build birthday flow off the loyalty app's birthday event with a live points balance
Build points-earned, tier-up and reward-redeemed flows off their platform events
Define VIP segment by order count with a capped extra send and quarterly offer
Reward VIPs with exclusivity and status, not broad discounts
Structure tiers around milestones and status, message the top tier least
Integrate reward redemption into checkout and track redeemer vs non-redeemer repeat rate
Gate investment in VIP-specific programming on VIP revenue actually being the constraint
Build community only where a real shared activity already exists
Bundle a non-competing subscription perk into a loyalty tier gated by order frequency
founder_sees: The loyalty and VIP flow set, and whether the data supports building a VIP tier at all.

name: Build back-in-stock and post-delivery education triggers
what: Builds the back-in-stock alert (only from a real restock event) and the review-request send timed after delivery.
encompasses: Trigger back-in-stock emails only from a real restock event, never a fake one
Time the review-request email about 3 days after delivery
Hand review-request timing to the connected reviews app once one exists
founder_sees: The back-in-stock and review-request triggers, wired to real inventory and delivery events only.

name: Build and maintain the segmentation model
what: Builds the segments that every flow and campaign draws from: engaged audience, RFM tiers, buyer stage, VIP, win-back-potential, high-potential and location, scored against the brand's own base.
encompasses: Keep 1 master email list and 1 SMS list, send to segments not lists
Join every can-receive-marketing condition with AND, never OR
Build the core engaged segment from opens, clicks, orders and site activity
Set the engaged window by send type and list health, widen only for major sales
Score RFM against the brand's own base, not an external benchmark
Trigger win-back, replenishment and abandonment off RFM instead of a fixed day count
Build buyer-stage segments: non-buyer, first-time, returning, window shopper, abandoner
Build 4 lifecycle cohorts for subscription brands by purchase and subscribe status
Build win-back-potential and high-potential segments
Build location and predictive-value property segments
Rebuild dormant reach gradually with random samples, not one full-list blast
Push high-engagement segments to ad platforms for lookalikes (flag for the media buyer specialist)
founder_sees: The current segment list with sizes, and which ones are stale or overlapping.

name: Build and maintain the campaign calendar
what: Plans the weekly non-flow campaign calendar in two layers (always-on baseline plus event-based peaks), keeping content mostly non-discount and rotating format.
encompasses: Set a sustainable weekly cadence and never skip a week
Plan in 2 layers: always-on baseline content and event-based peak campaigns
Keep content mostly non-discount, spend about 80 percent on broad-reach content
Never send 2 consecutive campaigns of the same content type
Rotate through a defined set of non-discount content frameworks
Use campaigns as a fast test lab, then port winners into flows
Reserve resends-to-non-openers for launches, restocks and sale-closers only
Set a graphic-to-text send ratio and pair email/SMS a fixed gap apart same day
Reject hyperpersonalized micro-segmentation as the default campaign strategy
founder_sees: The next 4-6 weeks of campaign topics and formats, ready for copy.

name: Write flow and campaign copy
what: Writes the actual email and SMS copy for an approved flow or campaign brief: subject lines, body, CTA, at a skimmable, tenth-grade reading level, checked against the brand record.
encompasses: Write for a 3-5 second skim at or below tenth-grade reading level
Lead with a pain or outcome headline, not a feature
Run the defined research routine before writing a new angle
Sell on at most 3 points, use reviews that each answer 1 objection
Hold discounts back to later emails in a sequence, lead with reminder and proof
Write short, curiosity-driven subject lines with hand-written preview text
Keep 1 consistent sender identity across flows and campaigns
Check every claim against the brand record before it ships
Treat AI-drafted copy as a draft only, edited before use
Close key sequences with a plain-text founder email
Reverse-engineer a strong reference email's structure, then write original copy
outputs: subject line and preview text options
founder_sees: The draft copy for the requested flow or campaign, with every claim traced to the brand record.

name: Design and QA email visual builds
what: Turns approved copy into the email build: 600px width, mobile-legible type, live text over locked images, one decision per section, compressed and alt-tagged images.
encompasses: Build at 600px width with mobile-legible text sizes
Put headline, short line, big button and code above the fold
End every section on one path to a product page
Cap product blocks at 3-5 items per email
Keep offer, product names and footer as live text, never locked in an image
Give every image alt text with the offer and a deep link, compressed
Build a standard footer with unsubscribe, address, category links and trust icons
Vary layout and imagery between sends, matching the brand's real look
Choose static or dynamic product blocks by catalogue turnover
Use show/hide logic to personalise one email for several audiences
Test-send to desktop and mobile before scheduling
founder_sees: The built email, ready to schedule, with the pre-send checklist ticked off.

name: Run the deliverability and list-hygiene program
what: Monitors sender reputation and inbox placement, keeps the list clean, and runs the repair ladder when deliverability degrades, treating content quality as the first fix.
encompasses: Authenticate the sending domain and ramp DMARC from none to reject
Suppress spam marks, bounces and the unengaged segment monthly
Fix content quality before chasing technical fixes
Run a staged repair ladder when sender reputation degrades, keeping abandonment flows live
Run a seed-list inbox placement test alongside open rate
Send 1-3 plain-text-only campaigns a month and invite replies as deliverability signals
Suppress never-emailed and no-activity-in-a-year profiles on day 1 of a new program
Build a tighter engaged segment for an underperforming inbox provider
Review or suppress long-tenure SMS subscribers who never bought
Restart a dormant sending program at a low cadence
Remove money words from value-first newsletter copy
Track click, spam-complaint and unsubscribe rate, not open rate alone
founder_sees: The current inbox-placement and list-health numbers, and what to fix first if they are slipping.

name: Manage the SMS, WhatsApp and push messaging program
what: Sets the rules for every non-email channel: content scope, cadence, cost control, consent, and channel selection, including a WhatsApp pilot where SMS is costly.
encompasses: Reserve SMS for high-urgency, low-frequency news only
Start cadence conservatively, raise it only through a proven holdout
Adjust frequency by the product's purchase cycle and buyer state
Keep every SMS to 1 message segment, check the platform's counter
Reserve MMS for sends where the image proves a net profit gain
Capture phone numbers as an activate-the-offer step after email
Pilot RCS or iMessage business messaging as a holdout, not a default rollout
Choose the SMS platform on price and ESP fit, not AI feature pitches
Add push notification steps to flows where the brand has an app
Consider WhatsApp business messaging where SMS is costly and the market is mobile-first
Track click rate, unsubscribe rate, delivery rate and net profit per send
inputs: brand brain: markets and channel costs
founder_sees: The recommended channel mix and send limits by market, with the cost math behind each one.

name: Design conversational and two-way messaging flows
what: Designs two-way SMS, RCS and WhatsApp conversations that start with a reply-inviting question and hand off to a human at the first real reply.
encompasses: Start conversational SMS with 1 reply-inviting question inside an existing flow
Delay the first conversational text a few minutes after opt-in for a human feel
Hand the thread to a live person at the first reply
Answer long questions with a voice note or short video
Add an RCS add-to-calendar action for launches and drops
Answer conversational product questions with an RCS recommendation carousel
Turn conversation reply themes into stored zero-party customer facts
Use iMessage text effects for a small set of specific moments
founder_sees: The conversational flow design, and the point at which it must hand off to a person.

name: Run the lifecycle testing and experimentation program
what: Prioritises and specifies A/B and holdout tests across flows, campaigns and channels, and enforces test hygiene so results can be trusted.
encompasses: Decide every test's winning metric as placed-order rate or revenue per recipient
Prioritise tests by revenue impact: flow delay first, CTA colour last
Test plain text against a fully designed version of the same message
Duplicate every downstream email onto both branches of a flow-timing test
Test flow email 1's delay before touching content, on the highest-volume flow first
Test a predictive smart-trigger pop-up against fixed delay rules
Test first-person vs second-person CTA copy
Test simultaneous multichannel abandonment sends
Run an SMS holdout test once SMS spend passes a real threshold
Design every retention test with a named constraint, a pre-registered hypothesis and a decision rule
outputs: test spec (hypothesis, variants, metric, sample size)
founder_sees: The next test to run, its hypothesis and how it will be judged.

name: Diagnose lifecycle metrics and run the monthly health review
what: Reads the full metric chain before diagnosing a flow or campaign problem, separates traffic issues from flow issues, and produces the monthly lifecycle read-out.
encompasses: Set clean attribution: exclude transactional sends, bot clicks and Apple opens
Turn on anonymous visitor tracking so pre-signup activity feeds flows
Check site traffic before flagging a flow revenue drop as a flow problem
Diagnose an underperforming email by copy, structure or design layer
Run a mandatory monthly review to catch silent breakage
Treat platform attribution as directional only; use profit metrics for the real constraint
Track retention metrics beyond CSAT and NPS
Recompute every reported figure from raw numbers, never reuse a rounded claim
Log AI-referred and agent traffic share every month
Run a quarterly unbranded prompt audit for brand visibility on AI platforms
Label every vendor benchmark as a claim, not a fact, in every report
founder_sees: The monthly lifecycle numbers with anything that broke or drifted, and why.

name: Enforce lifecycle honesty and platform-integrity guardrails
what: Applies the fixed set of honesty rules to every lifecycle send before it ships: no fake scarcity, no hidden text, no fake sender, no copied competitor content.
encompasses: Never send a fake restock, sell-out or scarcity message
Never use invisible text tricks to pad an email
Reserve insecurity-anchor copy for angles the brand voice allows and the cause is true
Never fake a person or an automated message from a human
Use competitor emails and ads for layout and mood only, never copy them
Compute lifecycle metrics in code from exports, never estimate them
outputs: flagged line items for the founder
founder_sees: A pass/fail on every honesty rule for the send in question, before it goes out.

name: Design the WhatsApp commerce program for India
what: Designs WhatsApp-based cart recovery, order updates and COD-to-prepaid conversion for Indian buyers, where WhatsApp reach beats SMS and email.
encompasses: Design a 3-step cart recovery sequence (about 30-60 min, 12-24 hr, 48-72 hr) with a rising incentive
Send order-status milestones (confirmed, dispatched, out for delivery, delivered) over WhatsApp for opted-in India buyers
Confirm COD orders over WhatsApp to reduce return-to-origin
Offer a prepaid discount or COD-fee waiver over WhatsApp to shift COD buyers to prepaid
Choose WhatsApp over SMS for update channel based on audience and opt-in
Keep WhatsApp consent and opt-out handling separate from email/SMS consent
Route product catalogue and payment links through WhatsApp's native commerce features where available
founder_sees: The WhatsApp message sequences for cart recovery, order status and COD-to-prepaid, ready for template approval.

name: Design the post-purchase journey and touchpoint experience
what: Maps the customer journey after purchase, classifies each touchpoint by the Kano model, and decides where to fund delight versus where to just fix a broken promise.
encompasses: Decide the intended feeling for each post-purchase touchpoint before writing its copy
Fix effort and broken promises before adding any delight spend
Split the journey into service moments and discretionary moments
Fund 1 deliberate peak and 1 strong ending, not an even spread of spend
Find and fix the journey's negative peak before funding any new delight
Classify every touchpoint with the Kano model before budgeting a fix or delight
Plan for delight decay and rotate every funded delighter on a cycle
Require every journey map to name at least 1 touchpoint it will change
Run a full persona journey-mapping session with Kano classification and a peak-end map
founder_sees: The journey map with the one negative peak to fix first and the one peak worth funding.

name: Design the order-status and delivery communication experience
what: Designs the confirmation, shipping and delivery-estimate messages and the branded tracking page, aimed at cutting WISMO tickets under 5 percent of orders.
encompasses: Turn the order confirmation into an anxiety-reduction message, not a receipt
Send at least 3 proactive automated updates between order and delivery
Build the delivery estimate from real carrier and lane data, shown as a specific date
Hold delivery-estimate accuracy above 90 percent, counting overdue orders as misses
Keep transactional emails focused on the order; route cross-sell to marketing sends
Reach out proactively before the customer asks when a parcel stalls
Tell customers up front when a multi-item order ships in separate parcels
Give a short self-service window to edit delivery address or cancel before ship
Point every tracking link to a branded page on the brand's own domain
Build the tracking page with status, a recommendation, loyalty link and returns path
Instrument tracking-page clicks and linked orders separately from raw visits
Show landed cost before checkout on cross-border orders
inputs: brand brain: policies (shipping, returns, guarantee, EMI)

external_write.surface: ESP transactional templates / tracking page build

founder_sees: The order-status message set and tracking page design, with the current WISMO rate and DEA score.

name: Design the unboxing, packaging and insert program
what: Designs the physical unboxing moment: layered reveal, inserts, gift, and note policy, capped to a set share of product cost.
encompasses: Design the unboxing experience on purpose, as the journey's main peak
Give every order a standard insert, reserve handwritten notes for VIP or high value
Cap packaging spend at 2-5 percent of product cost, model insert cost at current volume
Layer the reveal, add a first-use guide with a QR to a short setup video
Match packaging materials and texture to the brand's one-line promise
Put an unconditional gift in the box, never a conditional discount code
Make handwritten notes item-specific and honestly produced, never falsely claimed
Avoid a cheap, irrelevant or clearance gift
Treat packaging as a filmable creative asset and track unboxing UGC volume
Offer gift wrap and a hidden-price gift receipt at checkout for gift orders
outputs: packaging brief (materials, insert copy, gift policy)
founder_sees: The unboxing and packaging design, with its cost as a share of product cost.

name: Design the returns, exchanges and refund experience
what: Designs the return and refund flow: speed targets, refund-vs-credit choice, self-service portal, and fraud and RTO controls for COD markets.
encompasses: Collapse the refund timeline; measure request-to-initiation and initiation-to-receipt separately
Offer a clear choice between refund to original payment and store credit, never silent substitution
Measure fraud losses and cash-flow impact before scaling faster or instant refunds
Give returners a self-service portal with keep-it-or-donate refunds for low-value items
Publish the returns policy where shoppers see it before buying, checked against law per market
Gate further returns work on returners' repeat rate matching or beating non-returners
Track return-to-origin rate for COD orders and confirm high-risk orders before dispatch
Track chargebacks and payment disputes as their own cost line
inputs: brand brain: policies (shipping, returns, guarantee, EMI)
founder_sees: The returns and refund flow design, and the fraud/RTO numbers behind any policy change.

name: Draft support reply templates and ticket-tagging rules
what: Writes reply templates for the common contact types, sets tagging and routing rules, and decides which contacts can be automated end to end versus drafted for a human.
encompasses: Write support reply templates for the 8 common contact types, checked for brand voice
Reduce effort in every service moment: one-touch resolution, no dark patterns
Over-recover every genuine service failure with a scoped human gesture, never a manufactured one
Give frontline agents authority for one-time exceptions on sympathetic cases
Build a staff checklist for known edge cases before they happen
Track first-contact resolution, CSAT and repeat rate for the failure cohort separately
Weight 'helped me when something went wrong' above generic friendliness when prioritising fixes
Establish cost-per-contact and return-per-contact baselines
Resolve the issue first, then offer at most 1 relevant recommendation
Automate high-volume, low-complexity contacts first, keep humans for complex cases
Write the brand's voice spec before turning on any customer-facing support bot
Give AI budget to genuine post-purchase help, not only ticket deflection
inputs: brand brain: policies (shipping, returns, guarantee, EMI)
outputs: reply template library by contact type
founder_sees: The reply templates and routing rules, and which contact types are safe to fully automate.

name: Run the review collection and response program
what: Times and words review requests across the post-purchase flow, thank-you page and insert, and drafts responses to reviews, honest and unfiltered.
encompasses: Ask for honest, unfiltered reviews across the flow, thank-you page and insert
Time the review-request email about 3 days after delivery
Hand review-request timing to the connected reviews app once it exists
Draft responses to new reviews, positive and negative, in brand voice
Flag any review response that would need a policy exception before it is posted
founder_sees: The review request queue and draft responses, ready to send or post.

name: Run NPS, CSAT and voice-of-customer surveys
what: Runs the voice-of-customer process, starting with owned data and staff input before surveying customers, and keeps a standing NPS/CSAT read.
encompasses: Start voice-of-customer work with owned data (tickets, reviews) and employee input before surveying
Run NPS, CSAT and post-checkout surveys on a fixed cadence
Feed survey findings into the touchpoint fix backlog with evidence attached
tools: tool: survey platform (Okendo Surveys or similar)
founder_sees: The current NPS/CSAT read and the top 3 things customers say are wrong, from their own words.

name: Score CX maturity and recommend governance changes
what: Scores the brand's CX maturity (random, intentional or differentiated), and checks new customer-facing tools against a written experience standard.
encompasses: Score store CX maturity as random, intentional or differentiated
Give the customer a standing seat in leadership and merchandising decisions (recommend the practice)
Run a 3-part CX review across strategy, measurement and people
Judge every new customer-facing tool against a written experience standard before adoption
Recommend a dedicated cross-functional CX owner reporting to leadership once maturity supports it
inputs: brand brain: org and ownership notes
founder_sees: Where the brand's CX sits on the maturity scale, and one governance change worth making.

name: Build retention, cohort and LTV economics reporting
what: Computes lifetime gross profit (not revenue), CAC targets, and cohort retention metrics in code from order and refund data, always with a stated time window.
encompasses: Report customer value as lifetime gross profit, never revenue, with a stated time window
Build LTGP from order-level revenue and refund lines, not an assumed margin
Count refunds in LTGP only, never in the CAC denominator
Set a CAC target from LTGP using a 2-3x ratio, by store scale
Forecast incremental customer volume before raising the CAC ceiling
Bound CAC with a floor and a realistic headroom case
Value customers and visitors by margin, not revenue or order count
Stop using Shopify's percent-returning-customers metric as a retention KPI
Report every retention metric by acquisition cohort, never blended
Build one core dashboard around LTGP, first-to-second conversion and top-20% share
Produce a standard cohort read-out with 3 written findings every cycle
Run a discount-cohort audit before scaling any promotion
founder_sees: The brand's real lifetime gross profit and CAC target, computed from its own orders and refunds, not an estimate.

name: Set the existing-customer marketing spend policy
what: Sets how much paid budget, if any, should target existing customers, and at what CPA ceiling, handing the number to the media buyer specialist to execute.
encompasses: Default to little or no paid spend on existing customers
Set the existing-customer CPA target at half or less of the new-customer target
Measure the marginal CAC of an existing-customer spend increase and pull back past target
Budget existing-customer spend as a dollar figure from frequency and audience size, not a spend share
inputs: brand brain: paid channel spend by audience
outputs: existing-customer budget and CPA ceiling memo (handoff to media buyer specialist)
founder_sees: How much, if anything, to spend on ads targeting existing customers, and the ceiling on cost per result.

name: Score churn and lapse risk and route to the right save program
what: Builds a churn-risk score from RFM decay, subscription pause events, unresolved support issues and engagement drop, and routes each risk tier to win-back, cancel-flow save, or a support follow-up.
encompasses: Score lapse risk from RFM decay and subscription pause/skip events
Cross-check the lapsed list against unresolved service issues before any win-back send
Move chronic skippers or pausers into the cancel-and-win-back flow
Track a failure cohort's repeat rate and CSAT separately to see if churn ties to service issues
Segment win-back by lapse reason and measure recovery per reason
outputs: routing rule to the owning flow
founder_sees: The customers most likely to churn this month, why, and which save program each one should get.

name: Design personalization and zero-party data capture
what: Designs quizzes and on-site personalization that change what the customer sees or gets, not just their first name, and measures it against non-quiz buyers.
encompasses: Make personalization change what the customer sees or gets, not just a first name
Earn personalization data through a value-adding quiz the customer knowingly answers
Keep the quiz short and measure it against non-quiz buyers
Balance personalization against discovery, seasonality and ongoing testing
Pair personalization with risk reversal or virtual try-on where the category supports it
Run a zero-party persona audit on the top and bottom 20 percent of customers
Tag customers by goal with a 1-question survey and target offers by tag
Reject hyperpersonalized micro-segmentation as the default; route real personalization into flows and on-site
tools: tool: quiz app (Octane AI or similar)
founder_sees: The personalization or quiz design, and whether it actually lifts AOV or conversion versus non-quiz buyers.

name: Direct on-site search and merchandising ranking rules
what: Sets the business rules for on-site search and merchandising ranking (intent and margin, not popularity alone) and flags friction for the Site specialist to fix. Overlaps with the Site specialist (09-CRO); this capability owns the ranking policy, Site owns the implementation.
encompasses: Prefer buying an existing search/merchandising app over building one in-house
Write the business objective and allowed signals before any AI ranking or recommendation model ships
Rank on-site search by intent and business goal (including margin), not popularity alone
Audit whether top search queries land the right item on page 1
Flag repeated logins and long page-throughs in cart/checkout/account for the Site specialist to remove
Free merchandisers from manual search/layout monitoring for assortment and supplier work instead

external_write.surface: search/merchandising app config (implemented by Site specialist)

founder_sees: The search ranking rules and whether top queries land the right product, with fixes handed to the Site specialist.

name: Design the offer's value proposition and positioning
what: Writes the offer as a full package (price, terms, proof, guarantee), scored against the value equation, built around the buyer's single biggest objection.
encompasses: Write the offer as a full package, not just a discount
Name whether the offer targets conversion, basket size or repeat purchase
Score the offer against the value equation before cutting price
Build the offer around the buyer's single biggest objection
Differentiate a commodity SKU's offer instead of cutting its price
Reposition a hero SKU into several offers by persona
Cut offer components buyers do not value after 90-120 days
Add value before cutting price; test a higher price with a positioning change
Name the offer with the buyer's outcome word, tested on the PDP and in the ad
Build a value comparison against a real alternative on the PDP before the price
Match the ad's offer to the landing page and checkout; keep it identical everywhere
Reinforce true promises under the buy box: shipping, cancel-anytime, delivery date
founder_sees: The offer package proposal, the objection it answers, and where it is not yet consistent across ad, page and checkout.

name: Model offer and discount economics
what: Builds the margin waterfall and contribution model for any offer or discount before it launches, so a founder red line on margin is never crossed by accident.
encompasses: Build the full margin waterfall for every SKU before any offer
Judge every offer on contribution per order and per visitor, never revenue or ROAS alone
Reset target ROAS and CPA whenever the offer structure changes
Model discount depth on units per order, not an assumed lift
Check how fast required ROAS rises before approving a deeper discount
Measure the brand's own sale-period efficiency lift before trusting a discount
Match a competitor or marketplace price only when landed cost supports it
Find the profit-maximising discount depth from the brand's own sale history
Score every upsell/cross-sell by incremental contribution, not take rate
Measure upsell lift against a holdout, not takers alone
Compute cannibalisation and set numeric stop rules before approving any sale
Convert every USD benchmark to the brand's own currency before using it
inputs: brand brain: COGS and landed cost
founder_sees: Whether a proposed offer or discount clears the brand's contribution and margin floor, in the brand's own currency.

name: Govern discount policy and price integrity
what: Sets and enforces the rules that keep discounting from training buyers to wait: frequency caps, conditionality, honest framing, and any founder red line.
encompasses: Cut flat, frequent discounting that trains buyers to wait
Never show a reference price or bonus value that is not real
Always show the full price next to any per-day or per-unit figure
Give a discount only in exchange for a bigger order, a subscription, or clearing stock
Limit flat discounts to 1-2 times a year, on high-margin SKUs or clearance only
Choose dollar-off vs percent-off framing by AOV and currency
Never let a sitewide sale equal or beat the subscriber discount
State the true compounded discount when stacking subscription and sale offers
Only use all-sales-final for genuinely non-returnable items, with a true reason
Use scarcity and urgency only when real, enforced and provable
Make the promotion or bonus expire, never the core product
Never let a discount violate a founder red line; escalate for approval instead
inputs: brand brain: policies (shipping, returns, guarantee, EMI)
outputs: pass/fail check on a proposed discount
founder_sees: Whether a proposed discount follows the brand's own discount rules, and which rule it would break if not.

name: Design bundle, quantity-ladder and tier pricing
what: Designs multi-pack ladders and bundles from the product's real use journey, with a justified reason for every tier and a pre-selected middle option.
encompasses: Map the product use journey to find bundle and bonus ideas
Build a buy-more-save-more ladder for a consumable or multi-unit product
Bundle the same product or a true routine, not a forced mixed assortment
Use 3 tiers with the middle one pre-selected as the default
Step the per-unit price down with each ladder tier
Keep a low-friction, full-price entry tier in every ladder
Give every ladder tier a real physical reason to exist
Show the per-unit or per-day price next to the total on every tier
Make every tier, including the deepest, clear the contribution floor
Read take rate per tier after launch and retune the ladder
Set cart thresholds from the order-value distribution, not the average
Unlock a product, sample or gift at the cart threshold, not only shipping
founder_sees: The bundle or ladder design, its take rate by tier, and whether every tier clears the contribution floor.

name: Design gift-with-purchase and bonus offers
what: Chooses gifts that help the buyer use the core product, sized and placed to lift the tier the brand wants to sell, never framed dishonestly.
encompasses: Choose gifts that help the buyer use the core product, not swag
Prefer a low-landed-cost gift over an equivalent-cost cash discount
Scale the gift with units and place it on the tier to be sold
Never gift more of the same product the customer just bought
Announce the gift at every step and require a claim action
Test any order-2 gift's payback before scaling it to every subscriber
Make bonuses practical tools or how-to content, not more reading
State bonus and kit values only at real, sellable prices
Size total bonus value to exceed the core product's price
Recover a free gift's value when the qualifying order is returned
Withhold a promised free gift on COD orders until collection is confirmed
Deliver a promised bonus unit in the second order, not the first
founder_sees: The gift or bonus design, its landed cost versus an equal-cost discount, and its payback test result.

name: Design upsell and cross-sell placements
what: Places upsell and cross-sell offers by friction level (cart, checkout, post-purchase), anchored high with a cheaper down-sell, reviewed for margin and compliance.
encompasses: Place upsell offers by friction level: cart, then checkout, then post-purchase
Anchor post-purchase upsells high, then offer a cheaper down-sell
Review checkout add-ons like shipping protection for margin and compliance
Use product samples in a later box as cross-sells, not onboarding sales emails
Offer a post-checkout upsell framed as completing the purchase, not new selling
founder_sees: The upsell and cross-sell placement plan, reviewed for margin and for anything that reads as a dark pattern.

name: Design the guarantee and risk-reversal offer
what: Costs and writes the guarantee (length, conditions, coverage, activation), and any second guarantee layer, so it removes real buyer risk without breaking margin.
encompasses: Cost the guarantee's net contribution before proposing it
Write the guarantee as if not X in Y we will Z
Decide length, conditionality, coverage and activation deliberately
Add a second guarantee layer that removes a different risk
Make the guarantee visible near the price and at checkout
Fix the PDP and reviews first if refund rate is high, before relying on the guarantee
Name the guarantee clearly and on-brand, not with boilerplate
Size guarantee length and conditions for high-ticket items from the returns-cost model
Offer store credit as an alternative to a cash refund
Start the guarantee clock on delivery, not on order date
Test the guarantee window length using the brand's own refund data
Publish a real support response-time promise near the guarantee
inputs: brand brain: policies (shipping, returns, guarantee, EMI)
founder_sees: The guarantee's wording and length, and whether it clears its own cost model.

name: Design the subscription offer, perks and cancel flow
what: Designs the subscription value proposition, perk gating, cadence flexibility and the cancel-flow save offer, so the reason to subscribe is stronger than a flat discount.
encompasses: Aim first orders at subscription when cohorts show a large LTV gap
Replace a flat 10-15 percent subscribe-and-save discount with a stronger reason to subscribe
Put subscription-only perks on subscription, keep one-time visible but small
Pre-select subscription among 3 options, 2 of them subscriptions
Set subscription take-rate targets from contribution margin
Match cadence and pack size to real use, let customers adjust it
Design a gift roadmap that lands at high-churn months, shown before purchase
Put a costed, reason-matched discount inside the cancel flow, not upfront
Add a founder video and clear reasons before the cancel offer
Keep cancel findable and completable in as few steps as sign-up
Cap pause, skip and delay; treat delay as delayed revenue, not a save
Move chronic skippers or pausers into the cancel-and-win-back flow

external_write.surface: subscription platform config / cancel flow build

founder_sees: The subscription value proposition and cancel-flow design, and the cash math behind the first-order discount.

name: Design and model the pop-up and first-order offer
what: Chooses the pop-up offer type and models its full economics (opt-ins, revenue, discount cost, ESP cost) before it launches, testing structure before assuming a winner.
encompasses: Run a real first-order offer in the pop-up, not a bare join-us or generic 10 percent
Limit first-order pop-up offers to 4 types: currency off, percent off, free gift, or credit
Test structurally different pop-up offers on equal traffic, judge by profit and LTV
Test mystery/exclusive framing against a stated value, do not assume it wins
Make the pop-up offer match the site's real offer, with 1 true combined number
Model the full pop-up chain: opt-ins, revenue, discount cost, and ESP cost
Frame a pop-up discount as store credit instead of a percent-off code
Gate added acquisition spend on an AOV x conversion-rate score
founder_sees: The pop-up offer to run, and the full profit math behind it, not just the opt-in rate.

name: Design referral and partner offers
what: Designs a give-X-get-X referral program for the repeat-buyer base and finds non-competing partner perks that cost nothing to give.
encompasses: Run a give-X-get-X referral offer for the repeat-buyer base
Partner with a non-competing brand for a no-cost subscriber or referral perk
Size the referral reward from the brand's own CAC so it stays a bargain, not a giveaway
founder_sees: The referral offer design and its expected cost per new customer.

name: Design payment terms, trial pricing and delayed capture
what: Designs installment/BNPL terms with a clear per-installment price, nominal-price trials that convert to full price, and delayed payment capture for trial periods.
encompasses: Offer installment or BNPL terms with the per-installment price shown
Offer a nominal-price trial that converts to full price after a set window
Delay payment capture until a trial period ends instead of charging upfront
Add a decide-by incentive and reminders to trial and sample offers
Proactively offer to extend a payment plan at the point cancellations cluster
founder_sees: The payment-terms or trial design, with the per-installment price shown honestly.

name: Run the offer testing framework
what: Sequences and isolates offer tests (structure before depth, one variable at a time), keeps a backlog, and pre-registers the read window and metric before launch.
encompasses: Prioritise testing offer structure before offer depth
Preselect the test metric before running an offer test
Hold creative and landing page constant when testing an offer change
Start by testing 1 offer element unless a full overhaul is the hypothesis
Keep a backlog of untested offer ideas; expect most tests to lose or tie
Re-test an offer after any change in traffic source or creative
Judge offer tests on gross profit and a repeat-cycle LTV window, not first-order results
Test a free sample or usage credit against an equal-cost cash discount
Hold a winning offer 6-12 months, then audit it against belief
Keep testing offers even though most variants will fail
Refresh a fatigued offer in order: creative, copy, wrapper, duration, then price
Treat a seasonal demand dip as a signal to test a new offer
founder_sees: The next offer test to run, its read window, and what a past winning offer's 6-12 month audit found.
